questions.explanation: The scapula is a flat triangular bone. Its spine divides posterior supraspinous and infraspinous fossae; its glenoid cavity articulates with the humeral head, while the acromion and coracoid are key processes.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Name the bones that constitute the pectoral girdle and upper extremity (including superficial markings).
questions.prompt: Name a landmark of the humerus labeled in the lecture.
questions.hint: Think proximal tubercles and distal articular surfaces.
questions.explanation: The humerus has proximal head and tubercles for articulation and muscle attachments, a deltoid tuberosity on its shaft, and distal capitulum/trochlea and epicondyles at the elbow.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Name the bones that constitute the pectoral girdle and upper extremity (including superficial markings).
questions.prompt: Name a carpal bone in the proximal row.
questions.explanation: The proximal carpal row runs lateral to medial as scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum and pisiform. The pisiform sits on the palmar surface of triquetrum.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Name the bones that constitute the pectoral girdle and upper extremity (including superficial markings).
questions.prompt: Name a carpal bone in the distal row.
questions.explanation: The distal carpal row runs lateral to medial as trapezium, trapezoid, capitate and hamate. The trapezium articulates with the first metacarpal at the thumb base.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Name the bones that constitute the pectoral girdle and upper extremity (including superficial markings).
questions.prompt: Name a landmark of the ulna listed in lecture.
questions.hint: Think proximal elbow and distal styloid.
questions.explanation: The olecranon and coronoid process bound the trochlear notch of the ulna, which articulates with the humeral trochlea; the styloid process is at the distal ulna.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the pectoral girdle positioning muscles.
questions.prompt: Name a pectoral girdle positioning muscle listed in lecture.
questions.explanation: Pectoral girdle positioning muscles move or stabilize the scapula: serratus anterior protracts it, rhomboids retract it, trapezius contributes to elevation/retraction/rotation, and pectoralis minor draws it anteriorly/inferiorly.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the pectoral girdle positioning muscles.
questions.prompt: Which muscle holds the scapula against the thoracic wall and protracts it?
questions.explanation: Serratus anterior holds the medial border of the scapula against the thoracic wall and protracts the scapula. Weakness can produce scapular winging.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the pectoral girdle positioning muscles.
questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies serratus anterior?
questions.hint: The nerve is among the brachial plexus smaller branches.
questions.explanation: The long thoracic nerve innervates serratus anterior. Injury can impair scapular protraction and produce winging of the scapula.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the brachium and antebrachium movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Name a muscle that flexes the elbow.
questions.hint: Three muscles in the anterior antebrachium movement group.
questions.explanation: Brachialis is a strong elbow flexor; biceps brachii flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm; brachioradialis flexes best with the forearm in a neutral position.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the brachium and antebrachium movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Name a muscle that extends the elbow.
questions.explanation: Triceps brachii is the principal elbow extensor, while anconeus assists extension and stabilizes the elbow.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the brachium and antebrachium movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Name a rotator cuff muscle.
questions.explanation: The rotator cuff comprises supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis (SITS). Together they stabilize the humeral head in the glenoid during shoulder movement.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the brachium and antebrachium movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Name a muscle that laterally rotates the humerus from the lecture.
questions.explanation: Infraspinatus and teres minor are primary lateral rotators of the humerus at the shoulder; both are part of the rotator cuff.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the brachium and antebrachium movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Name a muscle that medially rotates the humerus from the lecture action list.
questions.hint: Both have medial rotation explicitly listed.
questions.explanation: Subscapularis and teres major both medially rotate the humerus. Subscapularis belongs to the rotator cuff, whereas teres major does not.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the brachium and antebrachium movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Which muscle assists deltoid in shoulder abduction?
questions.explanation: Supraspinatus initiates shoulder abduction and assists deltoid; deltoid provides much of the abduction force after initiation.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the brachium and antebrachium movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Name a muscle of brachium movement listed in the lecture.
questions.hint: Think shoulder movers and rotator cuff.
questions.explanation: These muscles move the humerus at the shoulder. Their actions differ: for example, deltoid abducts, pectoralis major adducts/medially rotates, and latissimus dorsi extends/adducts/medially rotates.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the hand and finger movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Name an anterior hand or wrist movement muscle from the lecture.
questions.hint: The slide lists one pronator and three wrist flexors.
questions.explanation: Anterior forearm muscles listed here participate in pronation or wrist flexion: pronator teres pronates, while flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus and flexor carpi ulnaris flex the wrist.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the hand and finger movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Name a posterior wrist or finger movement muscle from the lecture.
questions.hint: Extensor carpi muscles and extensor digitorum.
questions.explanation: Posterior forearm extensors include extensor carpi radialis longus/brevis and extensor carpi ulnaris for wrist extension, plus extensor digitorum for finger extension.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the hand and finger movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Which anterior forearm muscle pronates the forearm?
questions.explanation: Pronator teres pronates the forearm by rotating the radius over the ulna. Pronator quadratus also pronates, but this prompt asks for the named anterior muscle in the lecture answer list.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Identify the hand and finger movement muscles.
questions.prompt: Name an intrinsic hand muscle group named in lecture.
questions.explanation: Thenar muscles act mainly on the thumb, whereas hypothenar muscles act mainly on the little finger; both groups are intrinsic hand muscles.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Survey the blood vessels and nerves of the upper limb.
questions.prompt: Name a major terminal nerve of the brachial plexus.
questions.explanation: The five major terminal branches of the brachial plexus are musculocutaneous, axillary, radial, median and ulnar nerves. They distribute motor and sensory supply to the upper limb.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Survey the blood vessels and nerves of the upper limb.
questions.prompt: Name a smaller branch of the brachial plexus listed in lecture.
questions.explanation: Collateral brachial plexus branches supply shoulder-girdle and chest-wall muscles; examples include long thoracic to serratus anterior and thoracodorsal to latissimus dorsi.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Survey the blood vessels and nerves of the upper limb.
questions.prompt: Name an artery supplying the upper limb listed in lecture.
questions.hint: Follow flow from axilla to forearm.
questions.explanation: Arterial supply proceeds from subclavian to axillary to brachial artery; brachial divides into radial and ulnar arteries in the proximal forearm.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Survey the blood vessels and nerves of the upper limb.
questions.prompt: Name a superficial vein of the upper limb listed in lecture.
questions.explanation: Cephalic and basilic are major superficial upper-limb veins, often linked by the median cubital vein in the cubital fossa, a common venipuncture site.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only

questions.slo_text: Survey the blood vessels and nerves of the upper limb.
questions.prompt: Which spinal nerve roots form the brachial plexus?
questions.explanation: The brachial plexus is formed primarily from ventral rami of spinal nerves C5 through T1. These organize into roots, trunks, divisions, cords and branches.

validation.normalize: case, accents, punctuation and whitespace only
